correctness.rationale: The binary bit-prefix action is exact for all nondyadic states. The reflected +2/-1 chain has a verified stationary rational pgf, giving a nonnegative normalized density. Exactness of the doubling map and positive net bit deletion show total-variation convergence for any absolutely continuous start, proving uniqueness within that category. Partial-fraction and annulus identities establish thresholds for all p in (0,1/3); Laplace transforms establish the exponential limit. A standalone exact-rational checker passed 400 finite identities. Endpoint atom is separately stationary and excluded from uniqueness.

originality.rationale: Inspected random-map results contain a general constructive density formula and a more restrictive beta-series theorem, plus a symmetric one-zero-prefix Pelikan calculation, but do not state the asymmetrically contracted x/4-versus-doubling sharp p=1/7 integrability frontier together with the p→1/3 scaled exponential law. Real semantic-index and web queries were compared against closest results; the absence of a found match alone is not treated as proof of novelty. Priority remains subject to stronger broad literature.

value.rationale: A sharp boundedness threshold at p=1/7 lies strictly within the p<1/3 stationary-measure existence region; the theorem determines all finite-L^r thresholds and an explicit nondegenerate law for the near-critical logarithmic position. These are naturally interpretable qualitative changes and quantitative scaling constants, beyond confirming existence or merely specializing parameters.
